messages.author: 2d82c6a1f97843e6
messages.subject: Trouble with Omissions of Individuals
parts:
Hi Karl and community,

I'm having difficulty determining an issue when loading in my data using read_cross2. When the data is read in, I have animal genotypes that are omitted due to no sex/cross info. Is this due to individual genotype IDs not matching the pheno/covar IDs or would I need to do some manual changes using X/Yint data to delineate these individuals?

This is the output read_cross2:
"NAs introduced by coercionOmitting 1 markers that are not in both genotypes and mapsOmitting genotypes for 9 individuals with no sex/cross info."

As reference, this is my JSON file:
chr <- c(1:19, "X","Y")
write_control_file("HCa_DO1.json",
                   crosstype="do",
                   description="DO project batch 1-3a 7-20-2022",
                   founder_geno_file=paste0("GM/GM_foundergeno", chr, ".csv"),
                   founder_geno_transposed=TRUE,
                   gmap_file=paste0("GM/GM_gmap", chr, ".csv"),
                   pmap_file=paste0("GM/GM_pmap", chr, ".csv"),
                   geno_file=paste0("gm4qtl2_13_geno", chr, ".csv"),
                   geno_transposed=TRUE,
                   geno_codes=list(A=1, H=2, B=3),
                   xchr="X",
                   pheno_file="HCa_DOpheno.csv",
                   covar_file="HCa_DOcovar.csv",
                   sex_covar="sex",
                   sex_codes=list(F="Female", M="Male"),
                   crossinfo_covar="ngen", overwrite=TRUE)

Thank you for your time and insight!

Alanna

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with Omissions of Individuals
parts:
It's hard to tell without looking at the files. Could you share them with me?

As I understand the read_cross2 warnings:

- there were some values that were different then expected and converted to NAs. This is usually character strings in an otherwise numeric column.
- there is a marker that is in just the genotype data and not the maps, or vice versa.
- There are 9 individuals that are missing the sex covariate. It might be a mismatch of IDs, or it might be that they had a value different from F or M in the sex covariate column.

karl

messages.subject: RE: [SOCIAL NETWORK] [Rqtl2-disc] Trouble with Omissions of Individuals
parts: This usually happens to me when I use a data.frame for my sample genotypes. R helpfully adds an ‘X’ in front of samples that start with numbers and replaces spaces and punctuation with ‘.’. Maybe check the sample IDs in your sample genotype file and crossinfo file, paying special attention to any that start with numbers or have punctuation in them.
